project.name: common-health
project.description:
M18 phase 2: health contributors that make a Kubernetes READINESS probe mean something.
Spring Boot's readinessState is a servlet-container fact - it says "this JVM will accept an HTTP request", which M15 proved can be true while every @KafkaListener container in the process is stopped. This module adds two HealthIndicators that report the actual state of the Kafka machinery, so a readiness group can include them and kube-proxy can pull a pod that has stopped consuming out of its Service endpoints.
Deliberately its OWN module rather than a few classes inside common-web: psp-connector and webhook-notifier do not depend on common-web, and pulling common-web into them purely to get a health indicator would also have injected common-web's RFC-7807 GlobalExceptionHandler and correlation-id filter into two services that were never reviewed with them - a silent behaviour change smuggled in by a deployment task. Both Spring dependencies below are OPTIONAL, so this jar adds nothing to a service that does not already have them, and every bean is switched off unless the deployment explicitly asks for it (see KafkaHealthAutoConfiguration).
